levels.label: Nudge
levels.text: Where do the routes live? Open src/app.js and find the line for freeze_card. What stands in front of the handler today?

levels.label: Approach
levels.text: Express runs the functions on a route from left to right. Replace the old shared-credential check on the freeze_card route with your scope gate for the freeze_card action, and leave the other two routes exactly as they are.

levels.label: Near-solution
levels.text:
Import requireScope from ./middleware/require-scope.js, and give the freeze_card route `requireScope('freeze_card')` where `sharedCredential` was.

Restart the server (Ctrl+C, then npm run dev) before you run `npm run zoo`: the running server still has the old code.

reveal.referenceBrief:
CONTEXT: src/app.js defines three tool routes behind one shared credential. src/middleware/require-scope.js now has a correct requireScope(action).

TASK: Protect only POST /tools/freeze_card with requireScope('freeze_card'). The handler itself stays as it is.

CONSTRAINTS: get_balance and flag_transaction keep working with the old shared credential for now (hardening them is the homework). Do not change anything else.

VERIFY: Restart the server, then npm run zoo shows every answer as a hardened endpoint gives it, and npm run step -- 5 passes. The old broad token (npm run -s token -- broad) must now be a 403 on freeze_card.
reveal.approach:
One import and one changed line. The old token is still a real, signed token, so it now gets a 403 (valid, but not allowed), not a 401 (unknown or bad).

Do not forget the restart. "My change does nothing" is nearly always a server that is still running the old code.
commonMistakes: Not restarting the server after the change.
Hardening all three tools at once. The milestone says freeze_card only, and that is on purpose.
Putting requireScope after the handler, where it can never stop anything.
Editing the handler instead of the route.
